newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance takes backseat in Bombay rally.
newsitem.headline: Reliance takes backseat in Bombay rally.

text.p: Shares of India's largest private sector firm Reliance Industries lagged in a sharp rally at the Bombay exchange on Friday, traders said.
Reliance rose one rupee to 324.50 at the Bombay Stock Exchange amid volumes of over 3.97 million shares.
Rumours bubbled about a possible bonus share announcement by the firm ahead of its annual shareholders meeting on June 26.
The speculation has been around since chairman Dhirubhai Ambani hinted at the firm's last shareholders' meeting that a bonus issue could be forthcoming, analysts said.
"We always hear about the bonus rumour whenever the market needs to be given a push. Right now, the stock is being ignored," said a dealer at a local brokerage.
Reliance shares have jumped nearly 60 percent in 1997, favoured by massive capacity additions, high exposure to India's demand growth and increasing venturesin the oil, power and telecoms sectors.
"There has been a sharp run-up in the stock in the last fortnight. Action has temporarily shifted to other topline stocks," the dealer said.
